claims: C1: end user instructions may be included as part of a user message
C2: including end user instructions in a user message does not require quoting them with a specific format

concepts.name: end_user_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued by an end user of the product, as distinct from a developer instruction

concepts.name: user_message
concepts.gloss: M is a message in the conversation whose role is 'user'
concepts.inference: the source text names the 'user' message role; the message_role_definition/2 shared signature is the document-wide way to state a message's role, and this node's text presupposes that role without defining it

concepts.name: included_in_message
concepts.gloss: instruction I is included as part of message M

concepts.name: quoted_with_specific_format
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that is quoted with a specific format such as YAML, JSON, or XML

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule or instruction that carries the root level of instruction authority, the highest level, not overridable by system, developer, or user instructions
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; this node's source text does not state it

concepts.name: message_role_definition
concepts.gloss: message M has role R, where R is one of system, developer, user, assistant, or tool
concepts.inference: the shared-name signature defines this predicate; this node's source text refers to a 'user' message without defining the role relation

ontology.inference: the source text names the 'user' message role; the shared message_role_definition/2 signature is the document-wide way to state a message's role
ontology.gloss: M is a message with the user role
